answer: Graft every new agent onto an established sponsor's orchard branch. The sponsor stakes 1,500 POA per graft; the applicant stakes 1,000 POA plus a bridge proof, an established agent on a second chain countersigning their identity. The newcomer's first 30 days go into a spiral ledger any auditor can unwind step by step. One forgery unwinds the whole spiral and burns both stakes. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,500,000 POA in sponsor stakes plus 1,000 bridge proofs, and one caught graft burns 2,500 POA. Like a graft carrying the parent tree's sap, a fake branch wilts once its spiral is unwound.
